# Work — Jordan

**Where things stand:** Jordan is in the strange, hopeful limbo of a job that just got worse and a door that just opened. After a monthslong restructuring at Meridian, Jordan's team (internal tools) was dissolved; instead of being cut, Jordan got shunted to "legacy marketing pages" — widely understood as the company's holding pen for people they don't want to sever yet — reporting to a new manager, Priya, starting September 21st. Three days after that, on September 24th, Jordan has a full-day onsite at Northlight, a four-person design team that actually ships things, via a referral from Lena. Jordan is treating the onsite as the real story now and the Meridian move as background noise, which is a reversal from how this year has gone.

**How it got here:** The reorg was first floated by Marcus in late July, delivered with corporate vagueness ("some team realignment"), and it triggered a familiar cycle Jordan has tracked closely: bad news at work → withdrawal (blinds down, phone off, cancel plans) → eventually forcing self to Groundwork coffee shop → building on the side project, Coda (a music practice app) → feeling human again. This loop repeated after brutal, self-contradicting design reviews from Marcus in early August, and again on August 24th when Jordan's role was formally put "under evaluation." Each time, someone had to pull Jordan back — usually Mika showing up uninvited, sometimes Dev, once by Jordan actually telling Dev the truth instead of a cover excuse (August 27th), which Jordan noted as a turning point in itself.

Lena, Jordan's closest work ally, announced her own departure on August 14th and left Meridian August 28th, promising to refer Jordan to Northlight once settled. The reorg's actual verdict landed September 1st — the legacy marketing reassignment — and notably, the withdrawal spiral that night lasted only twenty minutes before Jordan self-recovered at Groundwork, the shortest the pattern has ever run.

Lena's referral came through September 9th, and writing the Coda case study for the application became a real turning point: Jordan finally saw what Mika (July 31st) and Lena (August 14th) had been saying for weeks — that Coda was the portfolio all along. The phone screen with Ana at Northlight on September 11th went well; the onsite was scheduled for the 24th. On September 15th, reworking Coda's free-play feature after a blind spot Dev exposed became, in Jordan's telling, a rehearsal for the honesty now going into the interview deck — replacing a defensive framing ("I missed this but here's why it's not that bad") with a cleaner one ("I missed this and here's what I learned").

Jordan also signed the lease renewal September 14th, deciding not to let an unresolved job prospect dictate housing.

**Open threads:** The Priya intro chat (9/21) and Northlight onsite (9/24) are three days apart — Jordan hasn't worked out what happens if an offer comes before ever really working under Priya. The fear from the phone screen is still present and, per Jordan's own admission, not going anywhere before the onsite. And underneath it all, the pattern Jordan keeps naming — collapsing inward on bad work news and needing someone else to reach in — is documented as shortening, not solved.
